Company: Scidell Pty Ltd, allied company of Multicom Resources Pty Ltd 
Location: St Elmo Site, Julia Creek QLD, Australia 
Employment Type: Permanent, Full-time 
Recruitment managed by: Yakr Pty Ltd

About the company:
Our client Scidell Pty Ltd is a scientific delivery alliancing company created to provide professional and cost-effective services to Multicom Resources Pty Ltd. Scidell’s multi-disciplined scientific and technical professionals operate from Brisbane and on-site to deliver major projects from initial study through to execution, commissioning, and ongoing operational support. 

Multicom Resources is on a mission to bring high-purity critical minerals to the world and become a reliable supplier for global technology manufacturers. Currently, Multicom is progressing the permitting, approval, and development of its 100% owned Saint Elmo Project, situated 25 km east of Julia Creek in Queensland's Northwest Minerals Province, focused on advancing the production of critical assets like vanadium and high-purity alumina. 

About the role:
As a Process Operations Engineer at Scidell, you will play a crucial part in the day-to-day production activities, site construction, plant commissioning, and ongoing operations. Working under the supervision of the Process Supervisor, you will bridge the gap between practical plant operations and technical process engineering. You will be responsible for operating machinery, monitoring multi-stage chemical processes, managing operational readiness, and optimizing plant performance. 
This diverse position is tailored to heavily develop your technical capabilities, setting up a clear career path toward process engineering design, plant operations management, or minerals processing project construction management. 

Key Responsibilities:
• Process Engineering & Deliverables: Develop and review process engineering deliverables and technical systems ensuring they meet strict company engineering standards and industry best practices. 
• Plant Performance & Optimization: Monitor and analyze production stages and overall plant performance; develop remediation plans for underperformance and identify continuous improvement opportunities. 
• Equipment & Process Operations: Start up, shut down, adjust, and operate plant machinery safely according to standard operating procedures (SOPs). 
• Operational Readiness & Commissioning: Assist with development of operational readiness deliverables, site construction activities, technical training systems, plant commissioning, and startup. 
• Process Control & Monitoring: Check, adjust, and maintain key operational parameters including temperature, pressure, flow rates, and chemical concentrations. 
• Quality Control & Inspections: Conduct regular routine inspections and quality control checks on products and materials to ensure compliance with quality specifications, assisting with troubleshooting deviations. 
• Maintenance & Troubleshooting: Identify, troubleshoot, and address basic equipment malfunctions or deviations, and collaborate with maintenance and engineering personnel to resolve complex issues. 
• Safety, Compliance & Records: Adhere strictly to the Site Safety and Health Management System, promptly report hazards, and maintain highly accurate records of process parameters, production data, and incident logs. 

Key Requirements:
• Education: Bachelor of Engineering (Chemical) or an equivalent relevant engineering qualification. 
• Experience: Minimum of 18 months of hands-on experience working within a chemical processing, production, or plant engineering role. 
• Technical Skills: Demonstrated experience in process monitoring, chemical plant operations, parameter adjustments, and troubleshooting technical systems. 
• Adaptability & Autonomy: Proven ability to work effectively in an autonomous role, multi-task, manage time efficiently, and adapt quickly to changing plant environments. 
• Location Flexibility: Previous experience working in a remote and regional location is highly preferred, alongside a willingness to work on site at Julia Creek. 
• Soft Skills: Strong communication and relationship-building skills to collaborate smoothly with internal team members, laboratories, and external vendors/suppliers. 

Why join Scidell?
Scidell offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge mineral processing projects while working in a supportive and collaborative environment. This role is uniquely structured to expand your cross-functional skillset across construction, commissioning, operations, and design, providing an exceptional foundational platform for career progression in the critical minerals sector.

How to Apply:
If you're ready to be part of a dynamic team at Scidell Pty Ltd, dedicated to innovation and excellence, we’d love to hear from you! Please submit your resume/CV, ensuring you highlight your relevant engineering experience and qualifications.

Scidell Pty Ltd is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds. While we appreciate every application, please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Eilbeck Cranes is an 100% Australian owned company operating in Australia for 118 years specialising in the design, manufacture and installation of all types of overhead cranes, hoists and winches.

We are renowned for technically superior cost effective solutions for our customers.
We are currently seeking a Mechanical Engineering Technician – Crane Systems Support to join our team in our Perth, Western Australia Office.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

1.	1.	Review mechanical drawings and engineering specifications of crane and winch components to identify appropriate replacement parts.
2.	Analyse RFQ requests and preparing technical quotations for engineered crane components.
3.	Assess mechanical tolerances, materials and compatibility of fabricated parts.
4.	Coordinate fabrication or machining of crane components with manufacturing teams.
5.	Maintain engineering documentation and spare parts technical databases for crane systems.
6.	Support engineering and production teams to ensure components meet design specifications and safety requirements.
7.	Develop spare parts data base for Eilbeck Winches
8.	Respond to requests for quotation (RFQ) for Eilbeck Winch spare parts and other parts from time to time
9.	Research in archived jobs to determine parts required for the RFQ
10.	Assist in the Spare Parts Division as requested from time to time
11.	Follow up quotation with customers
12.	Process awarded purchase orders into jobs
13.	Procurement of parts and/raw materials required for the Job. 
14.	Project manage the production of required parts along with other Eilbeck Division leads.  
15.	Ensure that work be performed, within agreed times and to an acceptable standard ensuring all work completed.
16.	Updating computer inventory
17.	Ensure parts invoicing is completed in a timely manner.

Bachelor BSC in Mechanical Engineering
Overhead Crane experience
Excellent verbal, written communication and organisational skills

If you believe you have what it takes and want to be part of a company that recognises individuals for their contribution and rewards them appropriately and are looking for a long term future and career please apply.
